items.note: Story 1: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose president 1889-1911, creamery built 1891.
Article VII: paid on butterfat by test, not weight; station test governs.
'under payment by weight, nothing that followed would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Teague as bookkeeper and Sill as Larrow Green buttermaker are in Section A. Loomis is named only as a source, not as secretary. Credited under the list-type core-fact rule (no REQUIRED line).
Son of Gideon is correct, but Section A says Selby Vose was manager 'from 1911' (Stories 4 and 6), not 1913. 1911 is a planted value.
Story 6: yearly 'station gain ... five and a quarter per cent, as usual', carried to the general account.
Ostrey Hollow station, 7 miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, first season on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, tested; bottle neck ruled for the 17.6 c.c. charge; cream to Larrow Green and skim back. Core fact present.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897.
Invoice table: 6 doz pipettes at 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
'0.19 ... flat in every month and season'; reads low 'in exactly the same proportion, every time, in every season'.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924; dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 7).
'the station test book in Keddie's hand, 4 May 1896 to 31 December 1924'.
1896 average 3.80 on borrowed glass, and 3.61 as the recorded average on the short glass, both inside Section A.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 then back to 3.61, question mark. (The lender is asserted here; that is penalized under A06.)
Story 8: Orra Keddie was Emmet Brant's sister; Emmet had the largest farm.
1919 circular present, but not Keddie's 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are. Both are bolded.
Died February 1934; test book impounded 1925, to the Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two scales always agreed.

1902 complaints present, but Story 3 says 'The Hollow tested 0.19 below the valley', and the valley/Larrow Green figure is given as 3.80. E11 rejects 0.17. This conflates the two gaps, which the key says loses the item.
Grigg committee, Jan-Mar 1908 only; hay finding reported as their conclusion.
200,000 lb on a test of 3.42; error stated to be proportional. Richer-herd consequence not drawn (unbolded).
Roy Brant lent the weigh book to Ivy in 1958; to Hazel on his death in 1962.
Cudd's cheese company at Alder Corners, Vessey County, 'over the ridge'. Redlow not named; credited under the core-fact rule.
1915-1930, four Bottom men hauling in the summer flush, to Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year.
Other county, Cudd's own uncondemned glass, and a book never compared with the station's: at least two elements.
Same cows read 3.80 over the ridge and 3.61 at the station (0.19). The run's own 8/10-season overlap count differs from the key's 16 (unbolded).
Same cows, same Bottom, same seasons, two readings; points to the instrument, not the land or the men; answers hay; cheese yield rules out water.
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter, took over in 1941 and copied the figures out for Ivy in 1958.
Section A names Strawn, the Ordell circuit and his 1936 retirement but gives no 1907 start. The run's only start year is 'from 1908' (Section F), a planted value.
Strawn's lactometer and his never finding water appear only in Section F; nothing in Section A.
12 June 1923, calibrated burette, whole lot condemned.
'wrote down the condemnation and drew no inference about the 26 years behind it'.
Order 28 June, reply 2 July, new glass July 1923, 1924 average 3.80; office treated it as 'a broken window'.
Crate to the loft; notebooks to the state office, then the Farland library in 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925, after the 1924 rise.
Frick board, 17 March to 4 May 1925, second and third sittings in the weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); 'no cause established'.
Four books listed, including Strawn's 1923 notebook recording the condemnation, never laid beside the test book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 before the finding; $3,800 'without admission'; charged to the station account (Story 6).
Award one-fifth of the loss (Story 8); charged to the station account, which carried the station gain line (Story 6).
Ivy b. 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, dairy husbandry graduate student at Farland with Vaught.
Section A lists what she gathered but never makes the point that these records had never been brought together.
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against 17.6 = 0.95.
3.61/0.95 = 3.80, proportional, 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923.
40M lb; 1,520,000 vs 1,444,000; 76,000 lb; $19,000 at 25c; 'sits in the ledgers as station gain'.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; no water, no theft; cleared 24 years after his death. The 35- and 33-year intervals are missing (list, core fact).
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan, with the 'great-niece' error resolved.
Second cousins, derived through first-cousin fathers.
A08: full vs half siblings 'left open', 'no document settles it', generation count unchanged. Correct abstention.
Gideon Vose, father.
Gideon's Article VII made the station test govern pay; son enforced the rule and blamed the farmers.
A01 asserted: 'the best evidence says none'; E32 'Resolution: no connection.'
Treats a family member's denial as outranking the talk, which is the opposite of the key's 'a family member's denial is not a record'. Gives one asserting narrator, not two.
0.95, 5%, one part in twenty.
76,000; 5.26% of credited, 5% of delivered; both denominators named.
$77.93 with line sum.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
26 years 1 month 11 days vs 25 full years 1898-1922, part years explained.
A02: 1896 intake cannot be determined.
Variable: the measuring glass/pipette.
Tester, herds, pasture, scales, bottles, acid held constant.
3.80 for nine weeks, back to 3.61 when the glass returned.
Rules out tester, water and land; limits: not the size of the shortfall, not which piece.
Ledger gain (Kyle/Teague/Sill), 1911 interval (Orra/Falke), 1924 new glass (Keddie's averages/Vose): three narrators.

Claims the three reasons rest on different records, but reasons 2 and 3 both rest on the station test book (Keddie's averages). Fails 'no two resting on the same document'. It does name reasons that survive without 1958.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question it? No.'
Answers the literal question 'No. ... Selby Vose did not know'; key: yes, the low testing was a known grievance from 1902 and the subject of his 1919 circular.
Signed the ledger sheets carrying the gain, wrote the 1919 water circular, pressed water in 1925: three of five.
A03 asserted: verdict that he did not know the fault lay in the station ('negligence, not knowing concealment').
E.g. Keddie start 1896 (E36), 1908 sampling Jan-Mar (E25), 1924 average 3.80 (E12), weigh book 1897 (E22), six farms (E23), crate in the loft (E9).
Pairs noticed and broken: 16.27 (Vaught/Chronicle) by the 0.95 fit; 12 July (Vose/Rundle) by the 28 June order; $77.39 (Ammon/Chronicle) by the line items; and more.
A04 (E44) and A10 (E1) correctly abstained; A06 resolved as 'Larrow Green' (E21).
Grigg r15, Duncan r18 1868/82, Ammon r20, Vaught r11, Nym swapped keepers.
16.72/17.6 = 95%, proportional 0.19 of 3.80, onset 1897 after the 1896 3.80, end 12 June 1923 with 1924 at 3.80, farms unchanged.
Water (Vose, Sill) defeated by the lactometer, Cudd's yields, and the same families at 3.80 in 1911/1924. The '1908' start is penalized separately.
Theft (Teague) defeated: the cream arrived heavier, not lighter.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nil in summer against a flat 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie suspected the glass'; Frick's account rejected.
150 words by count.
Invoice, weigh book, ledger, cheese-factory tests, inspector's notebook, test book.
No decoy adopted; no wrong headline figure.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 asserted as fact (Stories 4 and 6, B3)
Corruption: Strawn's circuit dated from 1908 ('lactometer tests at every visit from 1908', F2)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as 'no connection' (B4, E32)
Gullibility A06: 1911 measure asserted borrowed from Larrow Green (Story 4, D1, E21)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'never' questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: verdict that the manager did not know the tests were wrong (D3)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware, answered 'No' (F)
